title: Build the truthful public data contract and collection core
objective: Restructure the Python pipeline around a versioned public schema, honest source states, last-known-good storage, and a hardened unauthenticated Guba collector so later scoring and frontend tasks can rely on a stable interface.
forbidden_changes: Do not modify the accepted schema v2 contract without stopping and reporting an architecture issue.
Do not change frontend files, workflows, documentation, orchestration control files, or another task's handoff.
Do not present simulated Xiaohongshu data as live or include interactive-login collection in the public default path.
Do not implement T-002 scoring behavior changes beyond the minimal moves required to preserve current behavior.
Do not modify or merge into the default branch.
deliverables: Installable/importable mom_index package with stable collect, build, validate, and all CLI commands
JSON Schema v2 plus honest empty/degraded seed payload
Hardened Guba collector with optional proxy, row-scoped parsing, retries, and explicit failures
Last-known-good storage and privacy-preserving public export
Quarantined explicit-only simulated source and local-only Xiaohongshu paths
Pinned runtime and development dependencies, license, migration cleanup, and legacy pipeline shim
Atomic implementation commit and handoff report
acceptance_criteria: The package compiles under Python 3.11+ and all documented CLI entry points show help.
A forced collection failure still produces a schema-valid payload with unavailable source mode and no fabricated current reading.
A successful fixture/live collection path records timezone-aware provenance and a last-success timestamp.
Public export contains no author identities, cookies, credentials, raw record dump, or silently simulated data.
Duplicate committed frontend data is removed from the source-of-truth architecture and simulated public history is purged into non-public fixtures or removed.
Changes remain inside the declared write scope and are delivered as an atomic commit.
